title: Admin Heuristics Task Runner + Telemetry for Runbooks-as-Tasks
creator: Ethan Patel
description:
Goal: Build a lightweight, policy-aware task runner that executes ‘runbooks-as-tasks’ with operator-facing heuristics and rich telemetry. This ticket covers the engineering work to prototype the runner, wire end-to-end telemetry (trace + metrics + auditable action log), enforce idempotency and RBAC boundaries, and provide integration hooks for Slack/GitHub/opsctl. The runner should support declarative task steps, branching by observed signals (metrics/logs), and safe automatic rollback when preconditions fail.

Why now: current ad-hoc runbook executions are slow manual processes with little structured observability. Teams need a reproducible, automatable way to perform common admin actions while maintaining compliance and post-action analysis.

Deliverables:
- Task runner prototype (Go service + small CLI shim) that can load a runbook DSL and execute steps as atomic, idempotent actions.
- Telemetry schema (Spans, custom metrics, and action-level audit events) and a simple dashboard sample in Grafana.
- Example runbook library (DB failover, model rollback, scale-up) with policy gates.
- Integration layer for: Slack incident channel commands, opsctl run, and automatic PR creation for change logs.
- Automated post-run summary artifact (S3 link) and minimal postmortem template generation.
acceptance_criteria: Runner executes a declarative runbook with at least 4 step types (http, shell, graphql, noop) and retries are idempotent
Action-level audit events emitted and visible in the telemetry pipeline (trace id and action id correlated)
RBAC enforcement prevents non-admin users from executing destructive steps in the staging and prod policies
Slack command "/ops run <runbook>" triggers a dry-run and then a gated live run with confirmation flow
A Grafana dashboard shows per-run latency, failure rate, and cost estimate; sample dashboards checked into confluence link
Automated rollback path exercised in an integration test and recorded as an audit event

steps: Week 1: Spike DSL shape + core executor loop; implement idempotency tokens and tracing context propagation
Week 2: Implement policy gating + RBAC checks; add mock telemetry exporter and sample dashboard panels
Week 3: Integrate Slack dry-run and confirm flow; build CLI shim opsctl run wrapper
Week 4: End-to-end integration tests including simulated rollback; document runbooks and handoff to SRE
risk_mitigation: Isolate execution workers in a dedicated namespace with resource quotas. Sandbox shell steps by default using a safe wrapper and limit to preapproved commands. All destructive steps require two-step confirmation and a signed token for prod. Telemetry includes a hash of the runbook to ensure auditability.
notes: Prototype aims to be minimal: prefer observable, auditable actions over full orchestrator features. If prototype is successful, follow-up tickets will split the policy engine into a separate microservice and add encryption-at-rest for action payloads. Consider reuse of existing opsctl auth tokens to avoid building new SSO flows.
